take: Brent above $100 with the UK still dithering over Rosebank is the story that matters most: sanctioning delays on the largest untapped UK field, with over 70% of the country's oil already imported, simply entrenches the tightness that has driven Q3 crude prices and refinery margins higher. The freight and macro thread is the Gulf risk premium, with Houthi claims against pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline and Egypt's parliamentary vote to defend the kingdom sitting alongside Bahri's $451m order for three VLCCs at IMI, a reminder that tonne-miles and tanker demand are being priced off disruption rather than fundamentals. The inventory angle is refinery runs, with US utilisation averaging above 95% of capacity between May and September, the highest for those months since 1998, which leaves little slack for product cracks if crude supply tightens further. The cross-market link is gasoil versus bunker: Asia's warning that it needs $1trn a year to avoid the next energy shock and the $39bn added to the world's LNG bill from the Iran war both point to sustained middle-distillate and marine fuel demand, keeping product tanker earnings supported even as new chemical and product tanker capacity is ordered at GSI. Watch for any formal decision on Rosebank, further confirmation of the Saudi pipeline attacks, and the next EIA weekly run data for signs that utilisation is finally easing off its highs.

items.title: U.S. refineries have been running at very high rates in 2026
items.summary: The U.S. refinery fleet has run at higher-than-normal rates this year, with refinery utilization averaging more than 95% of capacity between May and September, the highest for those months since 1998. Tight global product supplies this year have boosted margins for petroleum products, particularly for diesel, incentivizing the increased run rates.
